subproblem.title: The closed-form radial map Φ takes values in [0,1]^P and in the (m+1)-skeleton
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, a ∈ Euclid P with |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 for all i, κ : (Fin P → ℝ) → ℝ such that for every u there is a finset s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and κ(u) ≤ u_i for all i ∈ s, and suppose Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P satisfies Φ(y)_i = a_i + (y_i − a_i)/max(r_i(y), κ(r(y))) for all y and i (real division with the convention x/0 = 0, as in Lean; the denominator vanishes only when r_i(y) = 0 and κ(r(y)) ≤ 0), where r(y) denotes the function j ↦ r_j(y) := max((y_j − a_j)/(1 − a_j), (a_j − y_j)/a_j) (= (y_j − a_j)/(1 − a_j) if y_j ≥ a_j, and = (a_j − y_j)/a_j if y_j < a_j). If y ∈ Euclid P satisfies κ(r(y)) > 0, then 0 ≤ Φ(y)_i ≤ 1 for every i, and there is a finset s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and Φ(y)_i ∈ {0, 1} for every i ∈ s.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (a : Euclid P), (∀ i, |a i - 1 / 2| < 1 / 4) → ∀ κ : (Fin P → ℝ) → ℝ, (∀ u : Fin P → ℝ, ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, κ u ≤ u i) → ∀ Φ : Euclid P → Euclid P, (∀ (y : Euclid P) (i : Fin P), Φ y i = a i + (y i - a i) / max (max ((y i - a i) / (1 - a i)) ((a i - y i) / a i)) (κ (fun j => max ((y j - a j) / (1 - a j)) ((a j - y j) / a j)))) → ∀ y : Euclid P, 0 < κ (fun j => max ((y j - a j) / (1 - a j)) ((a j - y j) / a j)) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ Φ y i ∧ Φ y i ≤ 1) ∧ ∃ s : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + s.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ s, Φ y i = 0 ∨ Φ y i = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(i) of the parent proof (Φ(x)_i lies between a_i and the end of [0, 1] on the side of x_i, and equals that end for the at least ℓ = P − m − 1 indices with r_i(x) ≥ κ(x)).
1. From |a_i − 1/2| < 1/4 we get 1/4 < a_i < 3/4, so a_i > 0 and 1 − a_i > 0. Put k₀ := κ(r(y)) > 0 and μ_i := max(r_i(y), k₀); then μ_i ≥ k₀ > 0 and μ_i ≥ r_i(y).
2. Bounds. Fix i. If y_i ≥ a_i: (y_i − a_i)/μ_i ≥ 0, and μ_i ≥ r_i(y) ≥ (y_i − a_i)/(1 − a_i) gives (1 − a_i)μ_i ≥ y_i − a_i, i.e. (y_i − a_i)/μ_i ≤ 1 − a_i; hence a_i ≤ Φ(y)_i ≤ 1. If y_i < a_i: (y_i − a_i)/μ_i < 0, and μ_i ≥ r_i(y) ≥ (a_i − y_i)/a_i gives a_i μ_i ≥ a_i − y_i, i.e. (y_i − a_i)/μ_i ≥ −a_i; hence 0 ≤ Φ(y)_i < a_i. In both cases 0 ≤ Φ(y)_i ≤ 1.
3. Skeleton. Apply the hypothesis on κ to u := r(y): there is s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and k₀ ≤ r_i(y) for all i ∈ s. Fix i ∈ s. Then r_i(y) ≥ k₀ > 0, so μ_i = r_i(y).
   (a) If y_i ≥ a_i, then (a_i − y_i)/a_i ≤ 0 ≤ (y_i − a_i)/(1 − a_i), so r_i(y) = (y_i − a_i)/(1 − a_i); since r_i(y) > 0, y_i − a_i > 0, and Φ(y)_i = a_i + (y_i − a_i)(1 − a_i)/(y_i − a_i) = a_i + (1 − a_i) = 1.
   (b) If y_i < a_i, then (y_i − a_i)/(1 − a_i) < 0 < (a_i − y_i)/a_i, so r_i(y) = (a_i − y_i)/a_i and Φ(y)_i = a_i + (y_i − a_i)·a_i/(a_i − y_i) = a_i − a_i = 0.
   Hence Φ(y)_i ∈ {0, 1} for every i ∈ s, and P ≤ m + 1 + |s|. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_i := max(r_i(y), κ(r(y))) satisfies μ_i ≥ κ(r(y)) > 0 and μ_i ≥ r_i(y).
Since r_i(y) ≥ (y_i − a_i)/(1 − a_i) and r_i(y) ≥ (a_i − y_i)/a_i, Φ(y)_i lies in [a_i, 1] if y_i ≥ a_i and in [0, a_i) if y_i < a_i.
The hypothesis gives s with P ≤ m + 1 + |s| and r_i(y) ≥ κ(r(y)) on s; there μ_i = r_i(y) and Φ(y)_i is exactly 1 or 0.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean type agree. Positive κ makes every relevant denominator positive. Both sign cases establish the coordinate bounds for arbitrary y; the supplied index set then gives precisely the required number of endpoint coordinates. No unstated cube or dimension hypothesis is used.
